ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Viet Nam AML/CFT and UBO governance: Law No. 14/2022/QH15 on Anti-Money Laundering of 15 November 2022, effective 1 March 2023; Decree No. 19/2023/NĐ-CP of 28 April 2023 implementing the Law on Anti-Money Laundering; Law No. 59/2020/QH14 on Enterprises, especially Articles 4 and 11 on beneficial owners and legal capital; Decree No. 01/2021/NĐ-CP on Enterprise Registration, as amended by Decree No. 02/2023/NĐ-CP, requiring UBO statements in the enterprise registration dossier; Decree No. 05/2019/NĐ-CP on Non-Cash Payments, as amended, establishing the licensing regime and legal capital for non-bank electronic money institutions; State Bank of Viet Nam regulations on customer identification, enhanced due diligence, and suspicious transaction reporting.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing, and constitutional documents of the ultimate corporate shareholder/beneficiary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registrar in the shareholder's country of incorporation (e.g., Companies House, ACRA, or commercial registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization via the Vietnamese Embassy/Consulate in that jurisdiction, preceded by local authority authentication; Hague Apostille is not available because Viet Nam is not a party to the Apostille Convention.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of each ultimate beneficial owner's valid biometric passport and proof of residential address
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority or the competent sub-national public authority issuing identification documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization following notarization and authentication by the relevant local authority at the issuing jurisdiction.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and economic source-of-wealth statement of the capital contributors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The licensed commercial bank maintaining the capital contributor's account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization of the bank's signature and seal, supported by local notarization of the bank officer's authority.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney appointing the local incorporation agent and legal counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: All proposed directors and ultimate beneficial owners executing the power
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If executed abroad: Consular Legalization; if executed in Viet Nam: notarization by a Vietnamese Notary Public, subject to additional consular legalization only if the underlying document originated overseas.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP and sanctions screening of all proposed shareholders, UBOs, directors, chief compliance officer, and senior managers against: (i) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (ii) the U.S. Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List; (iii) the Socialist Republic of Viet Nam's national counter-terrorism and AML blacklist administered by the Ministry of Public Security; and (iv) global commercial PEP/sanctions databases (e.g., Dow Jones Risk & Compliance, Refinitiv World-Check). Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for PEPs, high-risk jurisdictions, and any beneficial owner using nominee or agency arrangements. Screening results must be documented, escalated, and retained for at least five years in accordance with Law No. 14/2022/QH15 and Decree No. 19/2023/NĐ-CP.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Cổng thông tin quốc gia về đăng ký doanh nghiệp (National Enterprise Registration Portal) — https://dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Articles 37-40 of Law on Enterprises No. 59/2020/QH14 and Article 11 of Decree No. 01/2021/NĐ-CP, a Vietnamese enterprise name must contain the legal-form identifier (e.g., 'Công ty trách nhiệm hữu hạn' or 'TNHH') followed by a proper name written in the Vietnamese alphabet. The name may include Arabic numerals, Vietnamese diacritics, and permitted symbols such as '.', '-', and '_'. A foreign-language name may appear only as a translation of the Vietnamese proper name and must be enclosed in parentheses; the Vietnamese-script name remains the registered name. All registration documents must be in Vietnamese; foreign-origin documents require certified translation and, where applicable, consular legalization.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may either (1) amend and resubmit the enterprise name within five business days of the rejection notice through the National Enterprise Registration Portal, or (2) file a formal written complaint with the Director of the provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) within 30 days of the rejection decision, in accordance with Law No. 02/2011/QH13 on Complaints. If the DPI Director fails to issue a resolution within 30 days, the applicant may appeal to the Minister of Planning and Investment, and thereafter initiate administrative proceedings before the competent People's Administrative Court. Name reservation is an administrative step only; the successful name is incorporated into the Enterprise Registration Certificate and no independent reservation certificate is issued.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for a licensed non-bank electronic money institution. The registered office must be a physical commercial premise with a street address in Viet Nam, evidenced by a lease or ownership document. A virtual office or mail-forwarding address will not satisfy the Department of Planning and Investment's enterprise registration requirement or the State Bank of Viet Nam's principal-place-of-business condition for payment intermediary licensing.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High: 70% estimated probability of unannounced physical on-site inspection by the State Bank of Viet Nam and/or the Department of Planning and Investment within the first 12 months following licensing, given the high-risk AML/CFT classification of electronic money issuance and digital wallet reserve management.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law on Enterprises No. 59/2020/QH14 (Articles 25, 26, 47, 48, 52, 56, 74-83); Law on Investment No. 61/2020/QH14 (Articles 37, 38, 39); Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP on Enterprise Registration (Articles 25, 28, 30); Decree No. 31/2021/ND-CP on Investment (Articles 30, 33); Law on Prevention and Combating of Money Laundering No. 14/2022/QH14 for the licensed payment scope.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) of the province or centrally administered city where the project is located; National Business Registration Portal (dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn) under the Ministry of Planning and Investment.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Enterprise Registration of a limited liability company (Form I-1/B-1 under Decree No. 01/2021/ND-CP); Application for Investment Registration (Form I-2 under Decree No. 31/2021/ND-CP); both accompanied by the consularized/notarized constitutional documents of the foreign investor.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a standard LLC under the Law on Enterprises; however, because the company will apply to the State Bank of Vietnam for a payment intermediary and electronic money license, minimum charter capital of VND 50,000,000,000 (approximately USD 2,000,000) must be fully paid in and maintained throughout operation under Decree No. 52/2024/ND-CP. At formation, the subscribed capital must be deposited into a blocked escrow account opened at a licensed commercial bank in Viet Nam and fully contributed within 90 days from issuance of the Enterprise Registration Certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [FULL NAME] LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY, RESOLUTION NO. 01/[YEAR], adopted on [date] by unanimous written consent of the Board of Members of [Full Name] Limited Liability Company (the Company) pursuant to the Company Charter and the Law on Enterprises No. 59/2020/QH14. WHEREAS: (A) The Company was issued Enterprise Registration Certificate No. [ERC number] dated [date] by the Department of Planning and Investment of [province/city] with charter capital VND [amount]; (B) The Company obtained Investment Registration Certificate No. [IRC number] dated [date]; (C) The Company intends to apply to the State Bank of Vietnam for a license to provide intermediary payment services and electronic money issuance, and must maintain minimum paid-in charter capital of VND 50 billion. NOW THEREFORE IT IS RESOLVED: 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND CONTRIBUTION: 1.1 The subscribed charter capital of VND [amount], divided among the members as stated in the Charter and the list of members, is ratified. 1.2 The legal representative is directed to open a blocked charter capital escrow account at a licensed commercial bank in Viet Nam and every member shall pay the subscribed capital in full within 90 days from the ERC date. 1.3 No reduction of capital, dividend distribution, or member withdrawal shall occur prior to the issuance of the State Bank of Vietnam payment intermediary license. 2. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: 2.1 The registered office and principal place of business of the Company shall be located at [full registered address], [ward], [district], [province/city], Socialist Republic of Viet Nam. 2.2 The General Director is authorized to execute the premises documentation, file the office location declaration with the DPI, and register any change of address with the DPI and the tax authority. 3. APPOINTMENT OF OFFICERS: 3.1 [Name] is hereby appointed General Director and legal representative of the Company under Article 56 of the Law on Enterprises. 3.2 The General Director is authorized to sign contracts, banking instructions, license applications, tax declarations, and labor documents on behalf of the Company. 3.3 The following officers are appointed: Chief Financial Officer [name]; AML Compliance Officer [name]; Head of Risk Management [name]; Company Secretary [name]. 3.4 The Company hereby adopts, as binding internal governance instruments, the Financial Risk Management Policy, the AML/CFT Policy, and the Information Technology Security Policy. 4. AUXILIARY RESOLUTIONS: 4.1 The General Director is authorized to engage external legal counsel, independent auditors, and technical vendors for the preparation and submission of the State Bank of Vietnam license dossier. 4.2 All actions necessary to obtain the company seal, tax code, social insurance registration, fire safety approval, and environmental clearances are ratified and adopted. This Resolution is made in original copies and shall be retained at the registered office, filed with the DPI, and submitted with the State Bank of Vietnam license application. Adopted by the unanimous written consent of all members on [date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Investment Registration Certificate (investment project approval for foreign-invested company)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) of the province or centrally administered city; submission made online through the National Investment Registration System or in person at the DPI one-stop desk.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The foreign investor submits the investment registration application on Form I-2 under Decree No. 31/2021/ND-CP, attaching the legal status certificate, audited financial statements proving financial capacity, the project proposal describing the electronic money and virtual IBAN business model, and the AML/CFT framework. The DPI appraises the project, consults the State Bank of Vietnam on the payment business segment, and issues the Investment Registration Certificate within 15 working days of receipt of a complete dossier. Foreign documents must be notarized in the home jurisdiction, consular-legalized by a Vietnamese diplomatic/consular office unless exempted under an applicable treaty, and translated by a certified Vietnamese translator.
required_dossiers: Application for investment registration (Form I-2, Decree 31/2021/ND-CP)
Certificate of legal status of the investing foreign entity (notarized and consular-legalized)
Audited financial statements or bank solvency report of the foreign investor for the most recent 2 years
Investment project proposal covering digital wallet issuance, virtual IBAN issuance, reserve management and payment clearing rails
Memorandum or letter of intent evidencing the blocked charter capital escrow arrangement at a licensed commercial bank
Power of attorney and passport/ID of the authorized representative of the foreign investor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DPI issues a written request for supplementation, the investor has 30 days to cure the deficiencies. If the IRC application is rejected, the investor may appeal to the provincial People's Committee within 30 days from the date of refusal, or refile after rectifying the project documentation and capital evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Enterprise Registration Certificate (company incorporation of the LLC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) Business Registration Division; online submission via National Business Registration Portal (dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the IRC, the investor prepares and submits the enterprise registration application on Form I-1 with the Company Charter, the list of members and capital contributions, member identification documents, the IRC, and the notarized decision of the members. The DPI verifies the company name, registered address, charter, and legal compliance, and issues the Enterprise Registration Certificate within 3 working days. The company acquires separate legal personality on the date the ERC is issued; the legal representative must sign the charter adoption and submit the list of members' capital contributions.
required_dossiers: Application for enterprise registration (Form I-1, Decree 01/2021/ND-CP)
Draft Company Charter of the limited liability company
List of members and the capital contribution schedule
Passports or IDs of all individual members and certified copies of legal entity members' incorporation documents
Investment Registration Certificate issued at Step 1
Resolution or written consent of members on capital contribution and nomination of the General Director/legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the dossier is incomplete, the DPI issues a deficiency notice within 3 working days and the applicant has 15 working days to supplement. A refusal may be appealed to the provincial People's Committee within 30 days or cured by refiling where the defect relates solely to the company name, registered address, charter inconsistency, or officer identification data.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Charter capital deposit in escrow and corporate bank account activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank operating in Viet Nam selected by the Company for the charter capital escrow and operating accounts.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Company opens the charter capital blocked escrow account by presenting the ERC, IRC, First Board Resolution, company seal, and passport documents of the legal representative and authorized signatories. Members transfer their subscribed contributions into the escrow account, with the bank issuing a capital confirmation certificate. After verification, the Company opens its main operating account, designates authorized signatories, and obtains internet banking credentials; the paid-in capital evidence is essential for the later SBV license application.
required_dossiers: Enterprise Registration Certificate and Investment Registration Certificate
First Board Resolution appointing the legal representative and authorized bank signatories
Company seal and seal sample declaration filed with the DPI
Passports of the legal representative and authorized signatories
Bank account application forms and AML/KYC customer due diligence forms of the Company
Charter capital deposit confirmation record
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the application, the Company shall correct the certified copies and signatory resolutions and re-submit within 5 banking days. Where the full charter capital is not paid within 90 days from the ERC date, the members become jointly and severally liable and the Company must file an amended list of members and capital schedule with the DPI; failure to cure may trigger compulsory registration cancellation procedures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration, company seal declaration, labor registration and post-incorporation statutory formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Department of Taxation and provincial Tax Department; Department of Labour, Invalids and Social Affairs; provincial Police (fire safety and public order); DPI Business Registration Portal for seal declaration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon ERC issuance, the tax authority automatically allocates a tax identification number through the electronic registration system. The Company declares the company seal sample to the DPI within 15 days of seal carving, executes employment contracts under the Labour Code, registers employees with the social insurance agency, and submits the workplace fire safety certification application to the provincial Fire Police. The Company also opens a retained payroll account for mandatory social, health and unemployment insurance contributions.
required_dossiers: Enterprise Registration Certificate containing the allocated tax code
Company seal sample declaration (Form II-6 under Decree 01/2021/ND-CP)
Labor registration list and individual employment contracts
Social insurance, health insurance and unemployment insurance registration forms
Workplace fire safety design dossier and fire safety compliance application
Lease agreement or ownership certificate for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax code is not automatically delivered, the Company may directly request activation from the provincial Tax Department. Delays in seal declaration or labor registration are cured by late submission with administrative penalty settlement; for fire safety, a measured enforcement notice may be addressed by submitting a completeness supplement to the provincial Fire Police and correcting physical fire-safety defects within the stipulated cure period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: State Bank of Vietnam license for intermediary payment services and electronic money operation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Bank of Vietnam (Payment Department and Banking Supervision Agency); one-stop submission office of the State Bank of Vietnam in Hanoi.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Company files the complete license application dossier with the State Bank of Vietnam under Decree No. 52/2024/ND-CP, covering the company governance documentation, paid-in charter capital confirmation, AML/CFT compliance program approved by the Board, technical system architecture for digital wallet and virtual IBAN issuance, payment clearing connectivity design, and a three-year business plan. The SBV appraises the legal, financial, technical and AML compliance conditions, consults where required with the central bank clearing department, and issues the payment intermediary license with a term of up to 10 years. The Company must not commence licensed money-issuing or wallet reserve activities prior to license grant.
required_dossiers: Application form for the license to provide intermediary payment services under Decree No. 52/2024/ND-CP
Enterprise Registration Certificate, Investment Registration Certificate, and notarized Company Charter
Resolution of the Board of Members approving the payment intermediary business operation
Bank confirmation of fully paid-in charter capital of at least VND 50 billion
AML/CFT policy and implementation procedures under Law No. 14/2022/QH14 and Circular No. 09/2023/TT-NHNN, including appointment of the AML Compliance Officer
Information technology and security architecture description for electronic money, digital wallets, virtual IBAN issuance, and reserve management
Three-year business plan and financial projections, including payment clearing and settlement risk management framework
Internal audit manual, corporate governance framework, and risk management manuals
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the SBV issues a deficiency notice, the applicant has 60 days to complete and refile the dossier. If the license application is denied, the Company may submit a new application after six months once core deficiencies are resolved; administrative appeal and court proceedings are available under the Law on Denunciation and the Law on Administrative Procedure Law No. 32/2011/QH13. During any appeal, the Company must remain inactive in the licensed scope to avoid unauthorized e-money issuance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: State Bank of Vietnam (Ngân hàng Nhà nước Việt Nam) as the monetary and financial licensing authority for electronic money and intermediary payment services; provincial Department of Industry and Trade for industrial establishment registration and the provincial Department of Construction for structural and occupancy clearance of the operations center and data facilities.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: License for Provision of Intermediary Payment Services covering electronic money issuance, digital wallet operation and virtual IBAN issuance (Giấy phép cung ứng dịch vụ trung gian thanh toán), issued under Decree No. 52/2024/ND-CP on non-cash payment services, together with the SBV registration of the electronic wallet product and payment clearing connectivity.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MONRE) and the provincial Department of Natural Resources and Environment (DONRE) of the project location.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category III (office-based financial technology and data center operation) — no full Environmental Impact Assessment report is required; the project is exempt from the EIA list under Annex II of Decree No. 08/2022/ND-CP, but the Company must complete the environmental protection commitment registration with the DONRE and file periodic environmental compliance reports covering the registered office, IT infrastructure, and waste handling.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with National Technical Regulation QCVN 40:2011/BTNMT on industrial wastewater for any auxiliary facility discharge; QCVN 19:2009/BTNMT and QCVN 20:2009/BTNMT on industrial and aggregate emissions for backup generators and HVAC; waste segregation, e-waste and hazardous waste transfer obligations under Law on Environmental Protection No. 72/2020/QH14 and Decree No. 08/2022/ND-CP; and QCVN 02:2019/BTNMT on dust and air quality for data center environments.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety design approval and fire escape certificate issued by the provincial Fire Prevention and Rescue Police under Decree No. 136/2020/ND-CP, covering the registered office, server rooms, and emergency evacuation systems; structural load and construction completion checkpoint by the provincial Department of Construction; occupational safety risk assessment, workplace health monitoring, and fire drill records under Law on Occupational Safety and Health No. 84/2015/QH14; installation of automatic fire alarm and suppression systems, backup power, and protected secure access zones for the data center and reserve management function.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: General Department of Taxation (GDT) under the Ministry of Finance of the Socialist Republic of Viet Nam; national tax administration portal: https://thuedientu.gdt.gov.vn (Electronic Tax Portal for e-filing/e-payment; corporate tax registration via https://dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn for enterprise registration integration).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-invested limited liability company must first obtain an Enterprise Registration Certificate (ERC) from the provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI). Following ERC issuance, the tax authority automatically issues a 10-digit or 13-digit Tax Identification Number (MST) through the business registration database. The company must then complete tax registration dossiers, including the registration of the head office and any dependent branches/sub-offices, via the electronic tax portal or directly at the provincial tax office. For value-added tax (VAT) purposes, the same MST serves as the VAT identification number; no separate VAT ID is issued. Foreign entities without a permanent establishment that derive Vietnamese-source income may need a tax registration code through the withholding agent or must follow the contractor withholding tax regime, depending on the structure. A licensed electronic money institution must also update its tax registration file to reflect the State Bank of Viet Nam (SBV) e-money license and any licensed payment intermediary activities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Viet Nam does not maintain a check-the-box pass-through election comparable to the U.S. regime. An LLC is always subject to entity-level corporate income tax (CIT) at 20% on worldwide taxable income if resident, or on Vietnamese-source income if non-resident. There are no hybrid mismatch elections for entities. Taxpayers may elect the VAT calculation method (deduction method or direct method) in accordance with Law on Value-Added Tax, subject to statutory conditions: the deduction method is generally mandatory for licensed electronic money institutions, as they are deemed to be engaged in taxable banking and financial ancillary services. Certain preferential regimes are available by election where the taxpayer qualifies for CIT incentives (e.g., high-technology enterprises, new investment projects), but this is a concession, not a classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) / Thuế Giá Trị Gia Tăng (GTGT)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general VAT registration threshold applies to enterprises: every entity established under the Law on Enterprises, including foreign-invested LLCs, is required to register, declare, and pay VAT regardless of turnover level. Foreign suppliers of digital services and other cross-border electronic services without a Vietnamese establishment are required to register, declare, and pay VAT under the foreign supplier e-registration portal (etaxvn.gdt.gov.vn) once they derive taxable turnover from Vietnam; specific threshold rules may apply under official guidance, but the general rule is mandatory registration for any taxable activity by an incorporated Vietnamese entity.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Viet Nam mandates electronic invoicing with a mandatory invoice issuance code (mã của cơ quan thuế) for businesses, including licensed financial institutions. The electronic invoice data must be transmitted in real time (or within one business day, depending on the invoice type) to the General Department of Taxation through the E-Invoice system. The system applies a digital stamping/clearance process: before an e-invoice can be legally used, the tax authority issues a tax authority invoice code after validating the invoice data via API integration. The invoice data format is XML per the official e-invoice technical specification. Electronic money institutions issuing virtual IBANs must integrate their invoicing systems with the tax administration's API and ensure compliance with Decree 123/2020/ND-CP and Circular 78/2021/TT-BTC on e-invoices, including authentication by digital signature. Fiscal data clearance is not a continuous transaction-level real-time control as in Italy or Hungary, but pre-clearance coding is a statutory condition for validity.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods and services supplied for export from Viet Nam, the 0% VAT rate applies if the following cumulative conditions are met: (i) the goods are actually exported out of Vietnam, or services are supplied to and consumed outside Vietnam (including services directly used for export production); (ii) the taxpayer holds a VAT invoice for the exported goods or services; and (iii) the taxpayer possesses a complete customs dossier, including the customs export declaration, a bill of lading or equivalent transport document, and an export payment/remittance document proving the consideration was received from a foreign party in a convertible foreign currency. For offshore services provided by an electronic money institution (e.g., virtual IBAN issuance or payment processing to non-resident merchants), the service must be consumed outside Vietnam and supplied to a foreign customer; however, banking, financial and payment intermediary services are expressly excluded from the zero-rating entitlement under the Law on VAT and are instead VAT-exempt (subject to output-input VAT treatment), meaning no 0% VAT is available for core e-money issuance or wallet management services unless the service falls within a specific export-service category approved by the tax authority and is performed for a foreign party with foreign consumption (e.g., certain software licensing or technical services, if separately carried out and properly documented). The general rule for financial services in Vietnam is exemption, not zero-rating; the electronic money institution must conduct a detailed service-by-service analysis and apply separate accounting between exempt financial services and potentially zero-rated export services.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Tờ khai hải quan điện tử) duly lodged and processed by Customs Authority of Viet Nam, with valid confirmation of export clearance
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill / other transport document evidencing physical export movement of goods
Commercial Invoice issued by the Vietnamese exporting company
Sales contract / purchase order with the foreign customer

Inward Remittance Certificate / foreign currency bank statement proving the receipt of export proceeds from abroad; for service exports, an offshore payment receipt and written documents evidencing foreign consumption (e.g., service agreement and certificate of use by foreign party)
For goods exported through export processing enterprises (EPEs) or CMT/processing arrangements, additional documentation under Circular 219/2013/TT-BTC and customs transit documents as required
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: For an electronic money institution, the General Department of Taxation and customs authorities perform post-clearance audits focused on fraudulent export VAT zero-rating claims. Penalties include: (i) retroactive VAT reassessment at the 10% standard rate (or non-deductible treatment for exempt financial services) for any improperly claimed zero-rated export treatment; (ii) interest on underpaid tax at the rate applicable to overdue tax obligations (currently 0.03% per day on the late-payment amount); (iii) administrative fines up to 20 times the tax under-declared amount in egregious cases, or up to VND 200 million per violation for non-compliant invoicing or failure to use tax-authority-coded e-invoices; (iv) criminal prosecution for tax evasion or smuggling if fraud is established, with penalties including fines up to VND 4.5 billion or imprisonment under the Penal Code for the statutory responsible officers; (v) clawback of refunds already paid, with mandatory interest, and suspension or revocation of VAT refund eligibility for 12 months in certain cases; (vi) for VAT refund fraud involving counterfeit export dossiers, the enterprise may be blacklisted on the tax authority risk management system and subjected to enhanced pre-refund audits for up to five years. The written authorization of the Viet Nam Chamber of Commerce? No, the GDT expressly prohibits refund claims based solely on bank statements, requiring authenticated customs declarations and FX remittance certificates; any mismatch among the customs declaration, bill of lading, and inward remittance certificate leads to automatic rejection and penalty.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) - Ngân hàng Nhà nước Việt Nam, operating under the Law on the State Bank of Vietnam No. 46/2010/QH12, the Foreign Exchange Ordinance No. 28/2005/PL-UBTVQH11, Decree 70/2014/ND-CP as amended by Decree 89/2019/ND-CP, and Decree 96/2024/ND-CP on external borrowing and lending. SBV is the sole licensing authority for banks and non-bank payment intermediaries under Decree 52/2024/ND-CP on non-cash payments and exercises exclusive FX administration, balance-of-payments statistics, and regulatory reporting authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Vietnam has accepted IMF Article VIII obligations, hence VND is convertible for all current-account transactions, including profit remittance, royalty payments, management fees, and service imports, subject to presentation of supporting documentation to a licensed bank (invoices, tax clearance certificates, audited financial statements). Capital-account convertibility remains restricted. FDI equity injections must flow exclusively through a Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA) opened at an SBV-licensed bank pursuant to Circular 15/2015/TT-NHNN as amended by Circular 02/2023/TT-NHNN. Foreign commercial borrowings require SBV registration under Decree 96/2024/ND-CP and must be drawn, serviced, and repaid through the DICA. Outbound portfolio investment by a Vietnamese EMI is severely restricted and effectively requires case-by-case SBV/MoF authorization. Dividend and profit remittance to the foreign corporate shareholder is lawful once annually after final CIT settlement, based on legally audited financial statements and retained earnings available for distribution; there is no dividend withholding tax on distributions to foreign corporate shareholders, but distributions to foreign individual shareholders attract a 5% final withholding rate after CIT.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Decree 70/2014/ND-CP (as amended) and the SBV's prevailing FX management directives, all export receipts of goods and services, including the EMI's cross-border service fees and e-money settlement commissions, must be repatriated to Vietnam and fully credited to a foreign currency account at an SBV-licensed bank within 30 calendar days of the contractual payment due date, or of the actual receipt date if earlier. The mandatory conversion-to-VND surrender ratio applicable to exporters is currently set at 0% by SBV's periodic FX policy decisions, but the DICA holder must still sell foreign currency to the licensed bank at the prevailing interbank rate whenever required by an SBV re-imposition of a positive surrender ratio (historically 30% under earlier regimes, with conversion mandated within 15 working days of a re-imposition order). The statutory timeline is not automatically waived for processing-zone enterprises; only documentary relaxation applies to EPEs, while the EMI is treated as an ordinary services exporter for these rules.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Joint Stock Commercial Bank for Foreign Trade of Vietnam (Vietcombank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account: DICA - Direct Investment Capital Account; Operational Account: multi-currency VND/USD/EUR current accounts

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Vietnam Joint Stock Commercial Bank for Industry and Trade (VietinBank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account: DICA; Operational Account: VND and FX settlement accounts

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Joint Stock Commercial Bank for Investment and Development of Vietnam (BIDV)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account: DICA; Operational Account: treasury and e-money reserve accounts

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Vietnam Technological and Commercial Joint Stock Bank (Techcombank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account: corporate settlement, virtual account sub-ledgering, and liquidity management

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Military Commercial Joint Stock Bank (MB Bank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account: VND and FX accounts, payment gateway settlement

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Vietnam Prosperity Joint Stock Commercial Bank (VPBank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account: SME-fintech settlement, e-wallet float accounts
Operational Account: FX current accounts, trade finance disbursement

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW-MEDIUM for direct offshore digital EMI operation without local licensing, and HIGH only for a locally incorporated and SBV-licensed non-bank payment intermediary. Legal constraints: no EU-style passporting exists in Vietnam; an offshore EMI (e.g., an EU/Singapore/U.K. digital bank) cannot issue virtual IBANs or hold VND e-money on behalf of Vietnamese customers without a subsidiary and an SBV license under Decree 52/2024/ND-CP. Foreign equity participation in a licensed payment intermediary service provider is capped at 49% of charter capital absent an international treaty exception. The offshore EMI may only act as a correspondent bank, a white-label technology vendor, or an authorized agent of the local licensee, provided it has no direct customer relationship and no domiciled VND liabilities. Any cross-border multi-currency virtual IBAN product must be conducted through the local licensee's foreign currency account and clear in the offshore EMI's jurisdiction, not through the domestic customer's e-wallet.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence and in-person KYC interviews are mandatory. For corporate account opening, the legal representative (Chairman of the Member Council or the General Director) must appear physically at the bank branch together with the Chief Accountant where applicable; the Law on Anti-Money Laundering No. 14/2022/QH15 and Decree 19/2023/ND-CP require face-to-face customer due diligence, including verification of original passports, visas, temporary residence cards, and notarized enterprise registration documents. Pure e-KYC remote account opening for foreign-invested LLCs is not accepted by Tier-1 Vietnamese banks. For DICA opening under Circular 02/2023/TT-NHNN, the authorized signatory must be physically present to sign the DICA agreement and submit the SBV-required certification of enterprise incorporation. Board resolutions appointing signatories and corporate seals must be legalized/notarized in accordance with Vietnamese law.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: opaque offshore beneficial ownership chain or nominee directors in the shareholder registry
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed UBO declaration under Decree 19/2023/ND-CP listing every individual with 25% or greater direct/indirect ownership or control; corporate organization chart showing shareholders up to ultimate natural persons; passport copies and source-of-wealth statements; notarized confirmation that no shell or nominee structures exist; audited balance sheet of the ultimate shareholder.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: high-risk product profile - issuance of virtual IBANs and unregulated e-money float without identifiable underlying trade
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SBV payment intermediary license under Decree 52/2024/ND-CP; e-money reserve management policy demonstrating 100% segregated VND backing in SBV-licensed bank accounts; independent AML compliance manual with transaction monitoring thresholds; daily reconciliation report between e-money outstanding and bank reserve balance; FATF travel-rule compliance statement for wire transfers; customer onboarding and sanctions screening procedures (OFAC, EU, UN, SBV blacklist).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: initial capital injection originating from a third-party remitter rather than the declared foreign investor
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Investment Registration (IRC) and Enterprise Registration Certificate (ERC) naming the exact remitter; board resolution approving capital contribution; SWIFT MT103 narrative showing DICA purpose code for direct investment and referencing IRC number; bank statement showing settlement in the DICA; audited financial statements of the foreign investor confirming legitimate source of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: rapid pass-through flows, round-tripping, or cross-border settlements inconsistent with the EMI's declared customer base
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Contractual master agreements with merchants and digital wallet users; know-your-customer (KYC) files for all material commercial counterparties; monthly transaction volume projections with statistical distribution; detailed description of each payment rail used (NAPAS, SWIFT MT103, SEPA credit); evidence that e-money issued does not create unlicensed deposit-taking; board-approved transaction limits and geographic restriction policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: inability to evidence physical office, local economic substance, and active business operations in Vietnam
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid lease agreement for Class-A office space in Hanoi or Ho Chi Minh City matching the IRC-registered address; payroll records and social insurance filings for resident staff; utility invoices; minutes of Board meetings held in Vietnam; tax registration certificate and monthly VAT/CIT filing acknowledgments; power of attorney to the bank branch manager for any post-accounting-period correspondence.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound routing follows a six-stage protocol: (1) obtain the Enterprise Registration Certificate and Investment Registration Certificate from the provincial Department of Planning and Investment or Export Processing Zone authority; (2) open a Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA) at an SBV-licensed Tier-1 bank under Circular 02/2023/TT-NHNN; (3) the foreign investor remits equity in USD/EUR via SWIFT MT103 using the standard payment narrative 'Direct investment capital contribution to [Company Name] under IRC No. [ID]'; (4) the Vietnamese receiving bank applies the SBV Balance-of-Payments purpose code for direct investment equity (capital contribution) and credits the DICA in foreign currency; (5) upon each drawdown, the EMI submits a utilization plan, and foreign currency may be converted to VND at the licensed bank's corporate exchange rate or held in the DICA for permitted foreign currency expenditures including import settlement, offshore loan repayment, and staff payments; (6) all subsequent changes to capital or shareholders require that the DICA be credited before any further disbursement, and no inbound equity wire may be credited to a general operational account. Third-party finance from non-shareholder offshore lenders must be preceded by SBV registration under Decree 96/2024/ND-CP and must use the DICA loan disbursement sub-account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade and service settlements are executed over the following clearing rails: (i) domestic VND disbursements to merchants and e-wallet counterparties settle real-time on NAPAS (National Payment Corporation of Vietnam) ACH rail, either via the acquiring bank's direct participation or through a Tier-1 partner bank; (ii) cross-border EUR/USD service fee payments and virtual IBAN payouts use SWIFT MT103 messages through the EMI's NOSTRO accounts at correspondent banks, with each instruction carrying the correct local FX purpose narrative and value-date discipline; (iii) high-value import settlement for infrastructure procurement (e.g., hardware wallets, data center services) is executed via documentary letters of credit issued under UCP 600, with issuance on MT700, amendments on MT707, and reimbursement between the Vietnamese issuing bank and the beneficiary's confirming bank over SWIFT; (iv) SEPA Credit transfers for European merchant payouts are originated by the EMI via the banking partner's pain.001 ISO 20022 message converted to an SCT in the EU/EEA clearing area, clearing through TARGET2/EBA CLEARING infrastructure; and (v) repatriation of profits, foreign loan repayment, and dividend distributions debited from the DICA with outward MT103 and supporting tax/audit documentation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot FX transaction (delivery in VND or foreign currency within T+2 per Circular 02/2021/TT-NHNN)
FX Forward contract with licensed bank, maximum tenor 365 days, requiring documentary evidence of underlying current or capital transaction exposure
FX Swap combining spot and forward legs between VND and USD/EUR, permitted tenor per SBV market convention and circular limits
Cross-currency swap (CCS) between VND and foreign currency executed with an SBV-licensed credit institution, subject to underlying loan or project cash flow documentation

FX Option (European-style call/put) with licensed bank, permitted only where the notional, strike, and tenor correspond to a genuine commercial or financial exposure of the EMI and are backed by formal hedging policy approved by the Board of Members
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are expressly NOT permitted for domestic corporates under the current SBV regulatory framework; all hedging must be deliverable and settled within Vietnam

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Declaration (Báo cáo tình hình thay đổi thông tin doanh nghiệp) confirming registered particulars, legal representatives, and owners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Business Registration Office under the Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) of the province of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 30 days after the anniversary of the date of issuance of the Enterprise Registration Certificate; one-off filing unless registered information changed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties of VND 5,000,000 to VND 15,000,000 (approx. USD 200 to USD 600) administrative fines; continued non-compliance may lead to enterprise registration suspension or strike-off after repeated violations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statement submission to tax authority (no separate corporate annual return to DPI; tax finalization acts as annual filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Department of Taxation (GDT) via provincial tax authority and, for licensed EMI, the State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) as regulator
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Corporate income tax (CIT) finalization return and audited financial statements due by the 90th day from the end of the fiscal year (i.e., 31 March for calendar-year taxpayers); annual CIT payment due no later than 90 days from fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late return penalty of VND 5,000,000 to VND 8,000,000 (approx. USD 200 to USD 320) and late payment interest at 0.03%/day on unpaid taxes; continuous failure risks compulsory tax assessment, freezing of bank accounts, and corporate suspension

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual license / registry maintenance filing and reporting for electronic money institution holding an SBV operating license
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Bank of Vietnam (SBV), Banking Supervision and Inspection Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Under SBV license conditions, annual submission of operating reports, financial statements, compliance reports, and internal audit reports within 90 days of fiscal year-end; ad-hoc reports on business changes within 15 days of occurrence
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: SBV administrative penalties up to VND 200,000,000 (approx. USD 8,000) for reporting breaches; non-compliance can trigger license suspension, conditional operation orders, or revocation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual labor-related and statistical compliance filings (annual workplace safety report, social insurance declaration finalization)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Department of Labor, Invalids and Social Affairs (DOLISA) and Vietnam Social Security (VSS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Social insurance contribution finalization by the 30th day from fiscal year end (i.e., 30 January for calendar-year); workplace safety periodic reports by 31 January
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Social insurance interest at 0.03%/day on arrears; administrative fines up to VND 75,000,000 (approx. USD 3,000) for underpayments or reporting failures; repeated violations subject to criminal sanctions for the legal representative

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies to all foreign-invested enterprises (FIEs) under Vietnamese law; additionally, independent audit is compulsory for payment service and electronic money institutions licensed by the SBV regardless of revenue or asset thresholds, including annual audit of financial statements in accordance with SBV regulations. Specific quantitative thresholds under Decree 59/2014/ND-CP (small enterprise exemptions) do not apply to licensed EMI/FIE structures unless wholly state-owned or expressly exempt by law.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Vietnamese Accounting Standards (VAS) as issued by the Ministry of Finance, with chart of accounts per Circular 200/2014/TT-BTC; entities with foreign ownership may apply IFRS for consolidated/reporting purposes only if separately permitted by the MoF; statutory entity books remain capable of producing VAS-compliant local financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Vietnam's Enterprise Law 2020/2021 and anti-money laundering regulations (Law on Anti-Money Laundering 2022), a limited liability company must maintain a Register of Members capturing exact share ownership percentages and any transfers of capital portions. Any transfer of membership capital requires updated registration to be filed with the Business Registration Office within 10 days of the transaction. There is no standalone 'annual UBO declaration'; however, the annual enterprise information report to the DPI and updated beneficial owner data in enrollment at the SBV for electronic money institution licensing must be current on each anniversary; AML-licensed fintech entities (EMI) are subject to ongoing STR and customer due diligence recordkeeping and must update the SBV with any change to beneficial owners within 15 days. As a specific SCOPE anomaly, if the EMI is treated as a licensed fintech with capital-less membership, the register changes are reported on a transaction-basis; an annual confirmation is nonetheless required with the annual DPI enterprise report.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 to USD 1,200 for licensed foreign-invested enterprise in Ho Chi Minh City or Hanoi including virtual office and annual corporate secretarial support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 to USD 12,000 for licensed EMI/E-wallet due to SBV-required audit comfort and accompanying regulatory filings

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Foreign-invested enterprises engaging in licensed fintech activities (electronic money institution) may qualify for standard CIT at 20% with no automatic sectoral tax holiday. High-tech or software production classifications under Decree 57/2025/ND-CP could support a preferential rate of 10% for up to 15 years and a 4-year tax-exempt/50% reduction period for qualifying new investment projects, subject to State approval. Small- and medium-sized enterprises may access 10% preferential rate thresholds. No general tax holiday applies to purely financial intermediary service income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 03/TNDN (Corporate Income Tax Finalization Return) and Form No. 01/TNDN (Provisional Quarterly CIT Return), both filed via the General Department of Taxation electronic portal (https://etaxvn.gdt.gov.vn) or the National Public Service Portal (https://dichvucong.gov.vn).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly provisional returns must be filed within 30 days after the end of each quarter; the annual finalization return must be filed within 90 days after the fiscal year-end (commonly 31 December). Any corporate income tax balance payable must be settled by the finalization deadline. Extension of finalization filing is not permitted; payment deadline may be extended only under specific administrative hardship rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 01 – [A] Business name and tax identification number (MST)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the LLC as registered in the National Enterprise Registration Database and the 13-digit enterprise tax code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Vietnamese tax identification number as granted by the local tax authority. A foreign-invested LLC uses its own MST; do not use the foreign parent's tax ID.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calendar year of the annual CIT finalization or specific fiscal year elected.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a different fiscal year is approved, indicate the actual year-end date and retain the approval letter for inspection.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 03 – Deductible business expenses (Chi phí được trừ)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total expenses deductible under Circular 96/2015/TT-BTC and Circular 25/2020/TT-BTC, including directly attributable operational costs of payment services and wallet reserve management, excluding non-deductible provisions and undocumented payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Vietnamese sourced deductible costs are included. Costs paid abroad to related parties must satisfy transfer pricing documentation and invoice formalities, otherwise the deduction is rejected.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 04 – Taxable income before carryforward (Thu nhập tính thuế)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revenue less deductible expenses, plus non-deductible items and other deemed income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-invested entity must compute taxable income on Vietnamese-source income arising from the licensed EMI operations; capital of foreign shareholders does not constitute taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses from prior years offset against current-year income, limited to 5 consecutive years from the loss year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must be evidenced by filed CIT finalization returns. No carryback permitted. Related-party transactions cannot artificially generate losses that are then carried forward without transfer pricing scrutiny.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory 20% or preferential rate if the activity meets the qualifying high-tech/new application conditions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident investor's home-country tax characteristics do not affect the Vietnamese rate. No separate branch tax; the LLC is taxed on all Vietnamese income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 07 – Foreign tax credit (Số thuế nước ngoài được khấu trừ)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for withholding taxes legally borne on foreign-source income or technical service fees derived through foreign permanent establishments, subject to the 20% absolute cap.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only applicable if the Vietnamese EMI recognizes foreign-source income. Controlled-foreign-company income of related entities is not creditable unless actually repatriated and declared.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 08 – Minimum tax top-up (Thuế tối thiểu toàn cầu bổ sung)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Pillar Two qualified domestic minimum top-up tax / income inclusion rule calculations where the consolidated group revenue of the ultimate parent is EUR 750 million or more; the qualified domestic minimum top-up tax applies at 15% effective rate from fiscal year 2024.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign-invested EMI that is a constituent entity of a multinational group within scope must file Form 04/GTDT and compute top-up tax under Resolution 107/2023/QH15 and Decree 132/2024/ND-CP. This does not apply to standalone low-revenue entities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 09 – Minimum substitute tax for licensing (Tài chính vi mô as special EMI licensing fee)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Separate regulatory licensing fees paid to the State Bank of Viet Nam for the e-money institution license are deductible business expenses, not substituted for CIT.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify that the EMI license fee has been paid through the SBV e-portal and recorded with the full VAT/corporate income tax deduction; failure to declare the license grant date to the tax authority triggers administrative penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties under Decree 125/2020/ND-CP, as amended: filing 01-30 days late attracts a fine from VND 2,000,000 to VND 5,000,000; 31-60 days late VND 5,000,000-10,000,000; 61-90 days late VND 10,000,000-20,000,000; over 90 days late VND 20,000,000-40,000,000. Late payment interest is 0.03% per day (approximately 10.95% per annum) on the unpaid tax. Failure to file the finalization return beyond 90 days can trigger forced assessment plus additional penalty up to 1.5 times the evaded tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Although domestic law does not impose a dividend withholding tax on post-corporate-income-tax profit distributions, the foreign parent must submit the following administrative documentation: (1) copy of the audited financial statements and tax finalization acceptance; (2) proof of full payment of CIT; (3) written profit distribution resolution of the Board of Members; (4) notification to the Ministry of Finance/State Bank of Viet Nam of the remittance if profit transfer exceeds USD 100,000 equivalent, using the SBV registration letter (registered with foreign-exchange form). All documents should be notarized and consularized where the recipient is in a non-APEC treaty jurisdiction. For jurisdictions with a dividend article, no treaty reclaim is necessary because domestic WHT is nil; however, if dividends are paid as interest-hidden distributions, a 5% FIE income tax or 25% contractor withholding could apply. Note: For capital gains on share sales to a non-resident, the non-resident seller is subject to 20% CIT on capital gain (net of cost), or 0.1% deemed revenue tax for indirect transfers.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory: Interest paid to non-resident lenders is subject to 5% WHT (final) under current withholding schedules; royalties paid to non-residents for software/technology/process IP are subject to 10% WHT plus VAT (5% on royalty base), reflecting total contractor tax of approximately 15%. Treaty rates: Interest is typically reduced from 5% to 10% under most Vietnamese DTAs but the domestic rate is already lower; royalty rates under treaties vary, often reduced to 10% (domestic already 10% plus VAT, so VAT remains). For an EMI fintech relying on proprietary wallet software or payment-processing technology licensed from abroad, treaty relief does not eliminate VAT/contractor obligations; a Foreign Contractor Tax registration and TRC-based exemption/reduction filing plus Vietnamese-source income declaration is required. The non-resident beneficiary must obtain a TRC from its home tax authority and submit it to the Vietnamese paying entity for the reduced rate; the payer is responsible for withholding the difference if the TRC is not submitted before payment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and Master File (Form 01, 02, 03/TK TNCN is not applicable; the relevant forms are 01/QLGN and 02/QLGN under Decree 132/2020/ND-CP) are required if the taxpayer has related-party transactions and its total related-party revenue is above VND 50 billion (approximately USD 2 million) and/or total related-party transaction value is above VND 30 billion. Additionally, the safe-harbour threshold: taxpayers with related-party revenue below VND 30 billion or with no related-party transactions must still prepare a TP risk assessment. For commonly controlled payments such as management fees, royalties, and interest, the standard country-by-country reporting threshold applies where the multinational group's consolidated revenue equals at least VND 18,000 billion (about EUR 750 million).
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Viet Nam applies Economic Substance Regulations through Decree 132/2020/ND-CP: transactions are recharacterized when the arrangement lacks commercial rationale and economic substance, especially in the EMI segment where intragroup SaaS fees, platform royalties, and digital wallet reserve management fees are subject to audit. For an electronic money institution, the absence of local decision-making, technology development, and risk management staff may lead to adjustments. Specifically, the QD 132 regulations require the taxpayer's business plan, employment of personnel, and asset ownership to be aligned with functions performed, risks assumed, and assets used. The State Bank of Viet Nam also imposes a physical license requirement and prudent reserve requirements; an EMI that merely collects funds and channels them to a related treasury company will be recharacterized as a conduit. Consequently, such a company may lose the benefit of deductions for intercompany commissions and royalties and may face additional CIT at 20% plus penalty interest.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing false invoices for software licensing or digital-marketing services from a related offshore entity, over-inflated management fees, using circular financing through the foreign parent and the wallet reserve account to strip profits while maintaining thin substance in Viet Nam.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Decree 125/2020/ND-CP and the Law on Tax Administration 2019, additional CIT assessed at 20%; a penalty up to 1.5 times the evaded tax for failure to apply arm's length pricing; late payment interest at 0.03% per day. In cases of intentionally mispriced IP royalties exceeding VND 100 billion, criminal tax evasion under Penal Code 100/2015/QH13 (Article 200) carries fines up to VND 4.5 billion and imprisonment for up to 7 years for responsible individuals.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General director and legal representative can be held personally liable for filing certified tax returns containing false entries; civil restitution to the tax authority; travel ban (exit suspension) applies to directors of delinquent taxpayers across the entire Vietnamese border; imprisonment up to 7 years for intentional evasion when the amount exceeds VND 100 million or where both large acts and complicity are proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operation of the e-money institution license with no employees in Viet Nam, no physical office, no local risk management, and intercompany contracts showing that all functional decisions are taken by the Hong Kong or Singapore parent; earning 90% of revenue from fees remitted out as technical service fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority may recharacterize the entire payment base and deny all intercompany deductions, impose a deemed profit margin under Decree 132/2020/ND-CP causing effective CIT of up to 20% on gross revenue, and revoke the enterprise registration through the licensing authority. The State Bank of Viet Nam may revoke the instant-payment/e-money license for failure to satisfy organizational and legal conditions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face administrative fines from VND 20 million to VND 100 million under Decree 98/2021/ND-CP for corporate governance failures; the corporate veil is pierced if the entity is shown to be an agent of the foreign parent: personal restitution for the full underpaid tax, prohibition from holding managerial positions in financial institutions for up to 3 years, and a travel ban until all liabilities are settled.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The EMI acts as a digital-wallet reserve manager and fails to submit suspicious transaction reports (STRs) to the State Bank of Viet Nam's Anti-Money Laundering Department, processes anonymous e-wallet transfers above the threshold, or allows the wallet reserve to be swept for cross-border payments to a sanctioned cryptocurrency exchange.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Anti-Money Laundering Law 2022 (effective 1 March 2023), administrative sanctions include fines up to VND 200 million for failing to report STRs; criminal money-laundering under Penal Code Article 324 applies when the underlying funds are the proceeds of crime: fines up to VND 3 billion and imprisonment up to 15 years for responsible persons. The entity's license is revoked for serious or repeated violations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The AML compliance officer and the general director are personally liable for failure to implement an internal AML program; can be subject to criminal imprisonment for money-laundering complicity, voidance of employment contracts, restitution of the laundered amounts seized via criminal confiscation, and entry into the public registry of prohibited financial-services managers. Personal travel bans apply to the chairman and directors pending the criminal investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Foreign Exchange Control / Illegal Capital Movement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the e-money wallet reserve to disburse loans to Vietnamese customers without a lending license, leaking Vietnamese Dong liquidity through overseas shell entities, or failing to remit profits via the registered bank account and official SBV foreign-exchange registration, thereby evading the FDI capital account regime.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Law on Foreign Exchange Administration 2005 and Decree 88/2019/ND-CP, fines range from VND 100 million to VND 200 million for operating a payment service without an SBV license; the transaction is void and funds may be confiscated; repeated violations lead to criminal penalty for illegal foreign-exchange brokerage under Article 207 of the Penal Code.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are subject to personal criminal prosecution for unlawful cross-border transfers, travel bans, confiscation of personal bank accounts, civil restitution for exchange losses, and imprisonment up to 10 years for organizing currency trading without permission.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Pillar Two GloBE Non-Compliance (for covered multinational EMI groups)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The foreign parent group with consolidated revenue exceeding EUR 750 million fails to register the Vietnamese entity with the GDT as a constituent entity, fails to file the top-up tax return, or organizes low-taxed reserves to be booked in Viet Nam while paying related royalties offshore to keep effective rate below 15%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Resolution 107/2023/QH15 and Decree 132/2024/ND-CP, penalties for non-filing of the qualified domestic minimum top-up tax return can reach VND 40 million plus 0.03% daily interest on unpaid top-up tax; for false statements to reduce the top-up, an administrative penalty of up to 1.0 times the omitted tax; the general tax administration penalty regime applies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the Vietnamese constituent entity are responsible for true and accurate GloBE filings; a deliberate false certification exposes the legal representative to a warning or fines up to VND 20 million, and where it generates a false refund claim, criminal tax-evasion liability under Penal Code Article 200 may attach with imprisonment up to 3 years. Travel bans are applied until the top-up tax is settled.
